subject: Endpoint FQDN ownership and client cert routing for private deployments
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: James Smith <james.smith@acme-financial.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Endpoint FQDN ownership and client cert routing for private deployments

Hi James —

Thanks for the sync earlier. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture a proposal for how we should handle FQDN ownership and client certificate routing for the VPC-connected private endpoints that Redwood will host inside Acme's peered project. Key decision points below, and a suggested timeline: 

1) FQDN ownership: Acme to delegate a subdomain (example: redwood-acme.internal.acme.com) to Redwood-managed private DNS in the peered VPC. This prevents split-brain between on-prem DNS and GCP Cloud DNS.

2) TLS termination model: we propose two-tier termination: mutual TLS at the customer-facing ingress (Acme-managed edge) with optional passthrough to Redwood sidecar when customers require end-to-end client cert validation. For most customers, edge mTLS + server cert on Redwood side is sufficient and reduces operational complexity.

3) Client cert routing: when Acme needs per-tenant client certs validated on Redwood, Acme will forward client certificate identity headers via an internal header set by the edge proxy (x-acme-client-id / x-acme-cert-chain). We will treat these headers as authenticated via the private network and trust the peered connection + signed forwarder assertion (signed JWT) from Acme.

4) CSR and key rotation: attach a CSR template (see attachment) for Acme's internal CA to sign short-lived server certs (90 days). We'll automate rotation with a shared runbook.

5) Auditing & logging: request that Acme enable VPC flow logs + private endpoint access logs and supply a weekly bundle for our Q/A pipeline for the first 30 days.

Proposed next steps: 
- Acme to confirm subdomain delegation and provide test NS records (target: +5 business days)
- We (Redwood) will prepare an NGINX sidecar config and test mutual TLS passthrough in our staging peered project (+10 business days after delegation)
- Joint smoke test and regression on a small tenant (+3 business days after staging readiness)

Let me know if you want this rephrased as a shorter mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Logan
--
Logan Wright
Director, Solutions — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: James Smith <james.smith@acme-financial.com>

Cc: Acme Security Team <secops@acme-financial.com>, GCP Networking <gcp-networking@acme-financial.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Endpoint FQDN ownership and client cert routing for private deployments

Logan —

This looks solid and addresses the concerns we raised. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Delegation: we can create the subdomain and add NS records, but our security team wants the delegation to be limited to a narrow set of RR types (A/AAAA/CNAME) — no TXT/CAA updates from Redwood. Is that acceptable?

- Header forwarding: SecOps insists on signed forwarder assertions as you noted. We'll send a sample signed JWT format. We will not allow raw client certs in headers without the JWT.

- Rotation: 90 days is okay but add an emergency revocation procedure (contacts + emergency key revoke steps).

I'll loop in our network engineer (see GCP networking) to schedule the initial NS change. Please circulate the runbook you plan to use for automated rotation and the exact NGINX config lines you need so we can pre-approve.

Thanks,
James
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: James Smith <james.smith@acme-financial.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Endpoint FQDN ownership and client cert routing for private deployments

James —

Thanks for the quick reply. A couple of operational notes from Redwood SREs: 

- NS restriction: restricting RR types is fine. We'll implement the delegation with only A/AAAA/CNAME write access. Redwood will serve no public records and will refuse TXT/CAA updates. We'll document the guardrail in the delegation manifest.

- Signed forwarder JWT: we'll require the header x-acme-forwarder-jwt with an issuer claim that matches acme:networking and an aud claim set to redwood:vpc-ingress. Token TTL should be short-lived (5m) and we'll validate signature against Acme's rotating JWKS.

- NGINX config snippet (for review):
  server {
    listen 8443 ssl;
    ssl_certificate /etc/ssl/redwood/server.crt;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/redwood/server.key;
    ssl_client_certificate /etc/ssl/acme/ca.pem;
    ssl_verify_client optional; # enforce via signed JWT check in Lua filter
  }

We'll attach a draft runbook and the CSR template to this thread (see attachments). Also adding Stephanie from partnerships — she will track the DocuSign for the delegation agreement.

-marissa
